title: Level 3 (Advanced) - D-24
notes:
West leads the ♠K against 5♣. There is a certain diamond loser. The contract will only fail if 2 heart tricks have to be lost and this will be possible only if West was dealt both the ♥K and the ♥Q. South can improve his chances by playing along elimination lines.

After winning West's spade opening lead with the ♠A, South should lead a middle club to dummy (retaining the ♣2) as both defenders follow. A spade is ruffed high and another middle club is played to dummy. South ruffs another spade high, eliminating that suit. The ♦A is cashed and South exits in diamonds.

If West wins this trick, he will be endplayed. A spade return will concede a ruff and discard, a heart return will hold South's heart losers to 1, and a diamond return will set up a diamond winner in the dummy (South must ruff high if an honor is played). South's club ♣2 can be played to dummy's ♣3 in order to access dummy's diamond winner.

For the defense to have a chance East must win the trick when South exits in diamonds. If East returns a diamond, South can guarantee the contract by discarding a heart. West is welcome to win the trick. As before, North has an extra diamond winner for South's remaining heart loser and the dummy can be reached with the ♣2 to the ♣3.

A diamond return by East is out and a spade return would concede a ruff and discard. East must therefore return a heart. South ducks and West wins the trick. West will have a safe exit card only if he was dealt 3 or 4 small diamonds. Dummy's remaining high diamond should be played and, if East produces the outstanding honor, South can ruff high and cross to dummy with the ♣2 to the ♣3 and fall back on a second heart finesse.

The recommended line of play never loses to the straightforward line of taking 2 heart finesses. The recommended line gains when West has both heart honors and the diamonds are distributed such that the defense cannot avoid being endplayed (the above diamond layout, for example).
